name: Eau Claire River (Altoona)

gaugeContext.note: No representative gauge has been reviewed for this below-Altoona-Dam trip. Chippewa River readings and the different Eau Claire River near Wausau are not substituted for its flow.

blurb: A short urban paddle on the lower Eau Claire River from River Prairie Park in Altoona to Phoenix Park at the Chippewa River confluence. This moving-water trip has rapids and is recommended for experienced kayakers. It is a different river from the Eau Claire tributary near Wausau.

sections.notes: An urban paddle from River Prairie below Altoona Dam to Phoenix Park at the Chippewa River confluence. Visit Eau Claire recommends experienced kayakers because of rapids. Check conditions and the Phoenix shoreline exit before launching, and arrange a vehicle shuttle. This trip ends at Phoenix; continuing toward Hobbs is a separate Chippewa River stretch.
sections.routeReview: The dotted line shows the general river course. Exact shore connections and passages through rapids, bridge openings or obstructions are not mapped.

measurement.reviewNote: Reviewed the complete tourism map and both overlapping halves against satellite imagery on 2026-11-06. The line follows the visible Eau Claire River corridor between the named accesses; it generalizes bars, banks and bridges. It ends near, not at, the shoreline points. Measured approximately 2.7476 miles; no landing connectors or survey accuracy are implied.

putInAccess.sourceName: Visit Eau Claire — River Prairie launch; City of Altoona parks plan
putInAccess.note: The unchanged coordinate comes from the public water-trail map embedded by Visit Eau Claire. Imagery shows the approach beside the bridge and a short path to the water, but the point sits inland of the visible shore. Keep an approximate access area and no verified river-bank claim. The city parks plan identifies the canoe/kayak launch as part of its river corridor; its draft date is April 2021, not a current field inspection.
putInAccess.directions: From River Prairie Drive, use the public parking and carry-in on the north side of River Prairie Park beside the Highway 53 bridge. Follow the signed river approach. This launch is downstream of Altoona Dam; the Area marker identifies the approach, not an exact water-edge landing.

takeOutAccess.sourceName: Visit Eau Claire — kayaking page and city water-trail guide
takeOutAccess.note: The tourism agency currently recommends Phoenix Park for launching. The unchanged guide coordinate lies just off the park tip in imagery, so retain an approximate access area. The park landmark at river mile 58.2 is distinct from the carry-in marked 58.1.
takeOutAccess.directions: Carry through Phoenix Park to the access at the Chippewa–Eau Claire River confluence. The guide identifies the downstream park tip near the pedestrian bridge. Inspect the usable shoreline and current before launching; the Area marker is not a vehicle destination or an exact landing.

mapAuditNote: River Prairie–Phoenix has a reviewed map and river-course overview. Both landings are source-backed approximate areas, with exact shoreline connections still unconfirmed.
